label: BW-style / CLI-adapted

rubric_scores.evidence: The classroom is recognizable through its whiteboard, suspended ceiling grid, pale partition, dark floor, flag, wall fixtures and scattered debris. Damaged surfaces are simplified.
The author view preserves the board on the right, partition on the left, fixtures and flag at the far end, and yellow material on the right foreground floor.

The board, ceiling grid, wall fixtures and debris have broadly plausible relative sizes. The author view feels more distant and horizontally compressed than the reference, but does not establish a gross functional scale mismatch.
Light walls and board contrast with dark carpeting; yellow floor material and red-blue flag remain distinct. Colors are paler and debris more geometrically regular than the target.
Major content remains visible under soft illumination compatible with the reference interior. Heavy grain and a dark foreground reduce quality without making the required objects unreadable.
Complementary views reveal partition thickness, floor-object volume and changing spatial relationships, supporting a genuine three-dimensional scene.
Actual wall, board and insulation meshes have nonempty finite geometry, material slots and parent chains. Their groups resolve to mesh children, and assigned materials contain connected shader data.

dimension_scores.evidence: Distinctive classroom contents correspond, but the distant composition, rigid debris and simplified ceiling damage weaken the match.
Architecture and floor piles mostly read as supported. Partition connections and the rigid flag attachment are less convincing.
Main color groups survive, but warm walls and saturated yellow material become pale, while folded and broken shapes become clean slabs.
Severe render grain, uniformly clean geometry and rigid sheet-like objects diminish the abandoned-room appearance.
Principal left-right and foreground-background relationships remain intact, though spacing and composition differ visibly.
Objects remain functionally plausible; the board appears elongated and the yellow pile flatter and more regular than the reference.
Soft shading preserves legibility, but strong grain, weak material differentiation and uneven foreground illumination limit fidelity.
Most prominent contents are represented, including fixtures, flag, ceiling grid and debris. Ceiling cavities, board subdivision and irregular damage detail are substantially simplified.

same_model_bias_limit: Research and independent judge use Astra; separate sessions do not establish human independence.
